subject: Realtime token stream stall — urgent customer escalation and action plan
messages:
From: James Stuart <j.stuart@avasolutions.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime streams: tokens stop flowing for 8–20s after last deploy

Hannah —

We started seeing this right after Friday's runtime push (v2.14). During live agent sessions a subset of websocket connections experience a complete stop in token delivery for ~8–20s, then the stream resumes and finishes. It happens across two different regions (us-west, us-east) and affects about 3–4% of sessions but it completely kills our SLA for interactive use.

Attached is a short ws_session.log for one affected session and a high-level timeline. We also see elevated 502/504s during the same windows in our edge logs.

Can you confirm whether this matches anything you see on your side? We need an ETA on a mitigation — customers are starting to escalate.

Thanks,
James Stuart
Head of Platform
Ava Solutions

Attachments: ws_session.log (text, 48KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: James Stuart <j.stuart@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime streams: tokens stop flowing for 8–20s after last deploy

James — thanks for the report and logfile. I've looped in Dev (runtime) and Marissa (CS lead). We're treating this as a P1 given the customer impact.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Dev: can you triage the ws_session.log and collect corresponding server traces?
- Marissa: please prep a short customer-facing note (what we know, mitigation options, next steps).

We may propose a short-term mitigation: route affected sessions to the non-streaming fallback endpoint to avoid user-visible stalls while we investigate.

I'll update you within 90 minutes with preliminary findings.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, James Stuart <j.stuart@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime streams: tokens stop flowing for 8–20s after last deploy

Quick triage notes after an initial pass against the logs James attached.

What I see:
- Spike in token-generation tail latency on a subset of inference pods that correlates with the exact timestamps James sent.
- Corresponding growth in the runtime's re-send/backpressure counters and a handful of 500-series errors from the aggregator layer.
- No obvious OOM on the worker; kernel-level metrics show a CPU scheduling spike coincident with the stalls.

Attachments I've uploaded: collectd_snapshot.tar.gz (node metrics) and a trimmed service_profile.json with the request IDs. Also linked the internal runbook and the SUP ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4521

Short-term mitigation options (pick one):
1) Route affected sessions to streaming-fallback=false endpoint (no client-side chunking) — immediate but increases per-token cost and latency slightly.
2) Apply a runtime config rollback to v2.13 on a controlled canary subset (risk: rollback surface).

I recommend option 1 while we continue root-cause analysis; I'll start a live tracing session and surface traces in the ticket.

— Dev
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: EXEC: Token stream stall — need executive alignment + customer call prep

Marissa / Markus —

Escalating to exec: Ava Solutions (strategic customer, DEAL-9876) is seeing intermittent token-stream stalls after our v2.14 runtime rollout. They reported a 3–4% session hit, but customer impact is high because stalls are user-visible and break interactive flows. Dev has a triage in progress and recommends the non-streaming fallback as an immediate mitigation.

What I need from leadership:
- Decision: approve temporary fallback routing (option 1 from Dev) for the next 24 hours and a small customer credit (proposed: 10% for the impacted window).
- Exec presence on a 30-minute sync today at 09:00 PT with customer (Ava) to agree the mutual action plan and communication.
- Communications: a short public-facing note for the customer + a postmortem owner.

Severity rationale: affects real-time SLA; risk of churn if we don't offer a robust mitigation and clear remediation timeline.

Please respond with approval or alternatives; I'll hold the customer call tentative for 09:00 PT.

Thanks,
Hannah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, James Stuart <j.stuart@avasolutions.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EXEC: Token stream stall — need executive alignment + customer call prep

Hannah — approved.

1) Approve temporary routing to no-chunking fallback for impacted sessions now. Ask infra to implement a traffic policy to route ~5% of Ava sessions to the fallback and expand if needed.
2) Approve a 10% credit for the affected window; finance will issue a credit note pending a short incident write-up.
3) I'm joining the 09:00 PT customer call and will bring CS remediation notes. Markus will provide SLA guidance.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call summary: action items and next steps (Ava Solutions token stream stall)

Thanks to everyone who joined the 09:00 PT call. Summary and concrete action items below — keeping it brief for exec runbook.

What happened (short):
- After v2.14 rollout we observed a tail-regression on token emission for a small percentage of live websocket sessions that led to 8–20s stalls.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Traffic policy: routed all Ava sessions to streaming_fallback=false for 24 hours (implemented at 08:50 PT). This eliminated user-visible stalls for subsequent sessions.
- Customer credit: finance to issue 10% usage credit for impacted window (Marissa / Markus).

Ongoing RCA work:
- Dev to finish kernel/CPU-scheduling trace analysis and identify whether a scheduling regression or kernel interaction introduced latency in v2.14. Ticket: SUP-4521.
- Engineering to prepare a canary rollback of the specific runtime change if RCA shows a regression; otherwise craft a targeted patch.
- Postmortem owner: Dev Patel; initial postmortem draft due EOD Friday.

Artifacts attached: ws_session.log (customer file), collectd_snapshot.tar.gz (node metrics), service_profile.json (request ids).

Next check-in: I'll post updates to SUP-4521 and schedule a follow-up with Ava for 48-hour status.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above.
